title: Full faithfulness of the concrete affine section-limit functor
statement: Let X be a scheme and U an affine open whose open subscheme is Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For a quasi-coherent ideal J on U, let F be the concrete functor on coherent formal modules [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] obtained by taking the ModuleCat inverse limit of their sections on U (computed by pushforward along U inclusion followed by evaluation). Then F is full and faithful. This identifies morphisms of arbitrary formal systems; it asserts no comparison with completion of a coherent module.

source.place: Lemma 087W: quotient formula for the limiting module and affine Hom correspondence, steps 1-2 of the natural affine comparison

proof.text: Identify the affine open with its canonical spectrum. The affine formal equivalence realizes each system by its inverse limit, with surjective projections and ideal-power kernels.

Any linear map of limits carries each ideal-power multiple into the same ideal-power multiple. Descend it uniquely through the surjective projections and identify the resulting component maps with sheaf maps by the affine Hom correspondence.

Cancel the source surjective projection to prove compatibility of component maps with transitions. The resulting natural transformation induces the original limit map, since all projections agree. A transformation with zero limit map has zero components by the same cancellation; affine Hom faithfulness makes it zero. This proves fullness and faithfulness.

mathlib_searches.query: Coherent formal modules on an affine scheme are reconstructed fully faithfully from inverse limits of sections
The inverse limit functor from coherent adic systems on an affine scheme to modules is fully faithful
mathlib_searches.results: SheafOfModules.fullyFaithfulForget and Scheme.Modules.fullyFaithfulToPresheafOfModules concern forgetful functors, not section limits; no exact match.

General fully faithful functors reflect limits; LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective constructs quotient equivalences. No formal affine section-limit theorem. Local source search found Scheme.Modules.exists_hom_app_top_eq_of_isAffine, hom_ext_of_isAffine and the affine formal projection theorem; these supply the route for the remaining lemma.

Bridging it to this functor and reconstructing morphisms remains necessary.

theorem formalAffineSectionLimit_full_faithful (X : Scheme.{u})
    (U : X.Opens) [IsNoetherian U.toScheme] (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (J : U.toScheme.IdealSheafData) :
    (formalAffineSectionLimit X U J).Full ∧
      (formalAffineSectionLimit X U J).Faithful
